{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
{{About|the ruled surfaces|the minimal surface|Catalan's minimal surface}}
[[Image:Catalan surface.gif|right|thumb|300px| A Catalan surface.]]

In [[geometry]], a '''Catalan surface''', named after the Belgian [[mathematician]] [[Eugène Charles Catalan]], is a [[ruled surface]] all of whose generators are parallel to a fixed [[Plane (geometry)|plane]].

==Equations==
The [[vector equation]] of a Catalan surface is given by

:'''''r''''' = '''''s'''''(''u'') + ''v'' '''''L'''''(''u''),

where '''''r''''' = '''''s'''''(''u'') is the space curve and '''''L'''''(''u'') is the [[unit vector]] of the ruling at ''u'' = ''u''. All the vectors '''''L'''''(''u'') are parallel to the same plane, called the ''[[Directrix (rational normal scroll)|directrix]] plane'' of the surface. This can be characterized by the condition: the [[Scalar triple product|mixed product]] ['''''L'''''(''u''), '''''L' '''''(''u''), '''''L" '''''(''u'')] = 0.[https://books.google.com/books?id=K31Nzi_xhoQC&dq=catalan+surface&pg=PA279]

The [[parametric equations]] of the Catalan surface are [http://www.mathcurve.com/surfaces/catalan/catalan.shtml]

<math> x=f(u)+vi(u),\quad y=g(u)+vj(u),\quad z=h(u)+vk(u) \,</math>

==Special cases==
If all the generators of a Catalan surface intersect a fixed [[Line (geometry)|line]], then the surface is called a [[conoid]].

Catalan proved that the [[helicoid]] and the [[Plane (geometry)|plane]] were the only [[Ruled surface|ruled]] [[minimal surfaces]].
